examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For byte-addressable chips, n address pins select 2ⁿ byte locations; data-pin width determines bytes returned per addressed location. Separate chip-select bits from internal chip addresses. If low-order address bits drive chip selection, the chips occupy interleaved input addresses rather than contiguous ranges.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
Four 1 KiB byte-addressable chips use input bits A3,A2 for chip select, with all other bits as their internal address. What is the smallest external address selecting chip binary 11 at internal address zero?

**Answer: 12.** Internal address zero forces every nonselect bit to zero. Select bits A3=A2=1 contribute 8+4=12. Using 3072 would incorrectly assume the highest address bits select the chip.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Active-high versus active-low enable pins change decoder wiring. Count chip capacity in the addressed unit, not blindly from address-line count alone.

Do not multiply the address count by word width when counting address pins.
